functions.name: pxr::TfToken::TfToken
functions.description: Default-constructs an empty TfToken representing the empty string. Very cheap; no table lookup is performed.

functions.name: pxr::TfToken::Find
functions.description: Returns the existing token for s if it has been created previously; otherwise returns the empty token.

functions.name: pxr::TfToken::Hash
functions.description: Returns a stable hash value for this token based on its storage identity. Hash value remains constant as long as the token is in use in the process.

functions.name: pxr::TfToken::size
functions.description: Returns the length of the string represented by this token. Returns 0 for an empty token.

functions.name: pxr::TfToken::GetText
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the token’s null-terminated character data.
requirements: The returned pointer becomes invalid once this TfToken object is destroyed.

functions.name: pxr::TfToken::data
functions.description: Alias of GetText(); returns a pointer to the token’s null-terminated character data.
requirements: The returned pointer becomes invalid once this TfToken object is destroyed.

functions.name: pxr::TfToken::GetString
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the string represented by this token. For an empty token, returns a reference to a shared empty string.
requirements: The returned reference must not be used after this TfToken object is destroyed.

functions.name: pxr::TfToken::Swap
functions.description: Swaps the contents of this token with other in constant time.
requirements: other must be a valid TfToken reference (may alias this only if std::swap semantics are acceptable).

functions.name: pxr::TfToken::operator==
functions.description: Returns true if this token and o refer to the same interned string. Constant-time comparison.

functions.name: pxr::TfToken::operator!=
functions.description: Returns true if this token’s string does not equal o.

functions.name: pxr::TfToken::operator<
functions.description: Lexicographically compares this token and r. Provides a strict weak ordering for use in ordered containers.

functions.name: pxr::TfToken::operator>
functions.description: Returns true if this token is lexicographically greater than o.

functions.name: pxr::TfToken::operator>=
functions.description: Returns true if this token is lexicographically greater than or equal to o.

functions.name: pxr::TfToken::operator<=
functions.description: Returns true if this token is lexicographically less than or equal to o.

functions.name: pxr::TfToken::IsEmpty
functions.description: Returns true if this token represents the empty string.

functions.name: pxr::TfToken::IsImmortal
functions.description: Returns true if this token is immortal. A false result can become stale due to races; a true result is reliable.

functions.name: pxr::operator<<
functions.signature: std::ostream& operator<<(std::ostream& stream, TfToken const& t)
functions.description: Inserts the textual representation of t into the output stream.
requirements: stream must be a valid std::ostream reference.

functions.name: pxr::TfToTokenVector
functions.description: Converts a vector of strings to a vector of TfToken, interning each string as needed.
requirements: sv may contain any strings; construction may be relatively expensive for large inputs.

functions.name: pxr::TfToStringVector
functions.description: Converts a vector of TfToken to a vector of strings by extracting each token’s string.
requirements: tv may contain any tokens, including empty tokens.

functions.name: pxr::hash_value
functions.description: Returns the hash for x by delegating to x.Hash(). Suitable for use with Boost-style hashing.
requirements: x must be a valid TfToken reference.

data_types.description: A generic byte string with no required encoding or structure. May be empty or contain any characters, including whitespace, NUL bytes are typically not present in std::string content but any 8-bit values are acceptable. Used wherever functions accept std::string inputs without specific format constraints.

generators.generator:
import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets functions that consume arbitrary std::string values.
# Goals:
# - Produce valid, interesting strings covering: empty, ASCII words, unicode-like UTF-8,
#   long strings, repeated patterns, whitespace-heavy, comma/whitespace-delimited blobs,
#   edge lengths near small boundaries, and strings with punctuation.
# - Encourage duplicates and pairs for comparisons by embedding multiple segments that
#   fuzzers may split or reuse across FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls.
# - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.
#
# Output format:
# We return a single bytes blob that FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME read from.
# To supply multiple interesting strings to the stubs in one buffer, we encode
# a corpus of lines separated by newlines. Typical fuzzer harnesses pull sequentially.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

ASCII_PRINTABLE = (
    string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-.,:/\\|+*=!@#$%^&*()[]{}<>?~`'\""
)
WHITESPACE_SET = [" ", "\t", "\n", ","]

# Diverse sample unicode-like UTF-8 sequences (valid)
UNICODE_SNIPPETS = [
    " café ",              # Latin-1 supplement
    "日本語",               # CJK
    "🙂🙃😉",               # Emoji
    "προγραμμα",           # Greek
    "русский",             # Cyrillic
    "हिन्दी",               # Devanagari
    "🌟✨🔥",                # Emoji mix
]

# Some tokens often used in USD-like ecosystems to encourage interning collisions
DOMAINY_TOKENS = [
    "USD", "Prim", "prim", "xform", "material", "mesh", "points", "normals",
    "uv", "color", "visibility", "purpose", "default", "variant", "instances",
    "namespace", "Render", "Hydra", "SdfPath", "UsdGeom", "pxr", "token",
]


def _rand_ascii(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return "".join(r.choice(ASCII_PRINTABLE) for _ in range(n))


def _pattern(r: random.Random, base: str, min_rep: int, max_rep: int, noise_p: float = 0.0) -> str:
    reps = r.randint(min_rep, max_rep)
    s = base * reps
    if noise_p > 0:
        out = []
        for ch in s:
            if r.random() < noise_p:
                out.append(r.choice(ASCII_PRINTABLE))
            else:
                out.append(ch)
        s = "".join(out)
    return s


def _delimited_blob(r: random.Random, parts: List[str]) -> str:
    blob = []
    # Join with a mix of whitespace and commas, to trigger split logic in stubs
    for i, p in enumerate(parts):
        blob.append(p)
        if i + 1 < len(parts):
            sep = r.choice(WHITESPACE_SET)
            # Sometimes multiple separators
            if r.random() < 0.3:
                sep = sep * r.randint(2, 5)
            blob.append(sep)
    return "".join(blob)


def _make_segments(r: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    segs: List[str] = []

    # 1) Empty
    segs.append("")

    # 2) Small ASCII tokens
    for _ in range(r.randint(3, 6)):
        segs.append(_rand_ascii(r, 1, 8))

    # 3) Common domain tokens and duplicates to encourage equality
    picks = r.sample(DOMAINY_TOKENS, k=min(len(DOMAINY_TOKENS), r.randint(5, 12)))
    segs.extend(picks)
    # Duplicate some
    for _ in range(r.randint(2, 5)):
        segs.append(r.choice(picks))

    # 4) Unicode snippets and their repeats
    uni = r.sample(UNICODE_SNIPPETS, k=r.randint(2, min(5, len(UNICODE_SNIPPETS))))
    segs.extend(uni)
    for u in uni:
        if r.random() < 0.6:
            segs.append(_pattern(r, u, 2, 6))

    # 5) Whitespace-heavy pieces
    segs.append("\t\t\n   ")
    segs.append(",,,")

    # 6) Patterns and boundaries
    segs.append(_pattern(r, "A", 16, 64))
    segs.append(_pattern(r, "0", 1, 1))
    segs.append(_pattern(r, "ab", 32, 128))

    # 7) Medium to long randoms
    segs.append(_rand_ascii(r, 64, 200))
    segs.append(_rand_ascii(r, 256, 512))

    # 8) Mixed punctuation
    segs.append("--foo=bar,baz;qux|quux")

    # 9) Edge near 1024
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        segs.append(_pattern(r, "xyz", 300, 350, noise_p=0.05))

    # 10) Some exact-equality mirrors to trigger operator== path
    if segs:
        chosen = r.choice(segs)
        segs.append(chosen)

    return segs


def _assemble(r: random.Random, segs: List[str]) -> str:
    # Construct multiple lines so multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls get diverse inputs.
    lines: List[str] = []

    # Line 1: simple ASCII small
    lines.append(_rand_ascii(r, 0, 12))

    # Line 2: delimited blob from segments
    parts = r.sample(segs, k=min(len(segs), r.randint(8, min(32, len(segs)))))
    lines.append(_delimited_blob(r, parts))

    # Line 3: pure unicode cluster
    lines.append("".join(r.sample(UNICODE_SNIPPETS, k=r.randint(1, 4))))

    # Line 4: single long token
    lines.append(_rand_ascii(r, 100, 300))

    # Line 5: empty again
    lines.append("")

    # Line 6-9: a few repeats/mirrors to encourage equality/ordering
    if parts:
        lines.append(parts[0])
    if len(parts) > 1:
        lines.append(parts[-1])
    if len(parts) > 2:
        lines.append(parts[1])
    if len(parts) > 3:
        lines.append(parts[2])

    # Line 10: join many with commas to exercise split in vector stubs
    more = r.sample(segs, k=min(len(segs), r.randint(10, min(40, len(segs)))))
    lines.append(",".join(more))

    # Line 11: whitespace-separated
    lines.append(" ".join(r.sample(segs, k=min(len(segs), r.randint(6, 20)))))

    # Trim to size limit conservatively
    out = "\n".join(lines)
    if len(out.encode('utf-8')) > MAX_TOTAL:
        # Reduce by truncating the last long lines first
        trimmed: List[str] = []
        budget = MAX_TOTAL
        for line in lines:
            enc = line.encode('utf-8')
            if len(enc) + 1 <= budget:  # +1 for newline/join
                trimmed.append(line)
                budget -= len(enc) + 1
            else:
                # Truncate this line to fit budget-1
                if budget > 1:
                    # Take bytes slice on UTF-8 boundary: back off to valid boundary
                    b = enc[: max(0, budget - 1)]
                    # Ensure we don't cut inside a UTF-8 sequence
                    while b and (b[-1] & 0xC0) == 0x80:
                        b = b[:-1]
                    try:
                        trimmed.append(b.decode('utf-8', errors='ignore'))
                    except Exception:
                        trimmed.append("")
                    budget = 1
                break
        out = "\n".join(trimmed)
    return out


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    segs = _make_segments(r)
    blob = _assemble(r, segs)
    # Ensure UTF-8 encoding; std::string holds bytes, stubs treat as text
    data = blob.encode('utf-8')
    # Final guard
    if len(data) > MAX_TOTAL:
        data = data[:MAX_TOTAL]
    return data
